mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% over the signal period, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into consumer prices and thus will not trigger a hawkish Fed response.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < -2%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX forward returns are positive in > 60% of periods following a sharp INDPRO deceleration, indicating that markets are looking through the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 3%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates over the signal period, indicating that the economy is resilient to higher rates and that the restrictive policy will be short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates by more than 20% year-over-year, it signals a housing boom that will boost economic activity and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 30-year mortgage rates rise by more than 100 basis points over the signal period, indicating that financing costs will soon crimp housing demand and reverse the boom.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth decelerates sharply (3-month change < 100k), it signals a labor market slowdown that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall sharply over the signal period, indicating that the labor market slowdown is temporary and likely to reverse soon.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and the unemployment rate both rise together, it signals a 'stagflationary' environment of slowing growth and rising inflation that will depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The ISM manufacturing PMI rises above 55 over the signal period, indicating that the economy is still growing strongly despite the 'stagflationary' signals from rates and unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending growth accelerates by more than 5% year-over-year, it signals a consumption boom that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail inventories rise sharply over the signal period, indicating that the consumption boom is driven by overstocking rather than final demand and is thus unsustainable.
